templates.description: The LLM Hallucination Benchmark Task Type, Input, Label and Metrics used

properties.label: Property shape
properties.description: Task types in the context of LLMs refer to the specific applications or functions for which the models are used. Common task types include: 1) Generative QA (Question Answering): the model generates answers to questions based on its training data or provided context 2) Multi-Choice QA: the model selects the correct answer from a set of multiple-choice options 3) Detection: The model identifies specific elements or errors in the text, such as hallucinations or inconsistencies. These task types help evaluate the performance and capabilities of LLMs in various real-world applications.

properties.label: Property shape
properties.description: Task input in the context of LLMs refers to the type of data or prompts provided to the model to perform specific tasks. Task input types for LLMs include: 1) Question: a query that the model needs to answer 2) Paragraph/Document: a block of text or document that the model needs to summarize, analyze, or extract information from 3) Concept: specific terms or ideas that the model needs to explain or elaborate on 4) Query: a search or information request that the model needs to address 4) Paper: academic or research papers that the model needs to summarize or analyze 5) Task Input: general input related to a specific task, such as instructions or prompts 6) Entity: specific entities (e.g., names, places) that the model needs to identify or provide information about. These inputs guide the model in generating relevant and accurate outputs for various applications

properties.label: Property shape
properties.description: Task labels in the context of LLMs refer to the expected outputs or annotations that guide the evaluation of the model's performance. Common types of task labels include: 1) Answer: the correct response to a question or query 2) Passage: a specific section of text that the model needs to generate or identify 3) Response: the model's output in response to a given input, often evaluated for accuracy or relevance 4) Choice: options provided in multiple-choice tasks, where the model needs to select the correct one 5) Summary: a condensed version of a longer text, capturing the main points

properties.label: Property shape
properties.description: The task metrics used in the paper to evaluate large language models (LLMs) include: 1) LLM-Judge: uses a language model to evaluate the truthfulness and informativeness of responses 2) Human: human evaluators assess the accuracy and quality of the model's outputs 3) Accuracy (Acc): Measures the percentage of correct answers or responses 4) Balanced Accuracy: adjusts accuracy to account for class imbalance 5) Exact Match (EM): evaluates if the model's output exactly matches the expected answer 6) Precision: measures the proportion of true positive results among all positive results predicted by the model 7) Recall: measures the proportion of true positive results among all actual positive instances 8) F1 Score: balances precision and recall to provide a single measure of accuracy 9) AUROC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve): measures the model's ability to distinguish between classes 10) Pointwise Score: considers both positive scores for correct answers and negative penalties for incorrect ones 11) Likelihood: assesses the probability of the model generating the correct completion over non-factual completions 12) Score: general metric used to evaluate the overall performance of the model. These metrics help assess the factuality, faithfulness, and overall performance of LLMs.

templates.description: The LLM Hallucination Benchmark Attribute Factuality, Faithfulness, and Manual Input indication

properties.label: Property shape
properties.description: Factuality in LLMs refers to the accuracy and consistency of the generated content with real-world facts. It is divided into two subcategories: 1) Factual Inconsistency: this occurs when the LLM's output contains facts that can be verified against real-world information but present contradictions. 2) Factual Fabrication: this involves the LLM generating unverifiable facts against established real-world knowledge. Factuality is crucial for ensuring the reliability and trustworthiness of LLMs in real-world applications.

properties.label: Property shape
properties.description: Faithfulness in LLMs refers to the alignment and consistency of the generated content with the provided user instructions or input context. It is categorized into three subtypes: 1) Instruction Inconsistency: occurs when the LLM's output deviates from the user's explicit instructions 2) Context Inconsistency: it happens when the generated content is unfaithful to the provided contextual information 3) Logical Inconsistency: involves internal contradictions within the generated content, often seen in reasoning tasks. Faithfulness ensures that LLMs produce outputs that are consistent with user directives and the given context, enhancing their reliability and usability.

properties.label: measurementTechnique
properties.description: A technique, method or technology used in an Observation, StatisticalVariable or Dataset (or DataDownload, DataCatalog), corresponding to the method used for measuring the corresponding variable(s) (for datasets, described using variableMeasured; for Observation, a StatisticalVariable). Often but not necessarily each variableMeasured will have an explicit representation as (or mapping to) an property such as those defined in Schema.org, or other RDF vocabularies and "knowledge graphs". In that case the subproperty of variableMeasured called measuredProperty is applicable. The measurementTechnique property helps when extra clarification is needed about how a measuredProperty was measured. This is oriented towards scientific and scholarly dataset publication but may have broader applicability; it is not intended as a full representation of measurement, but can often serve as a high level summary for dataset discovery. For example, if variableMeasured is: molecule concentration, measurementTechnique could be: "mass spectrometry" or "nmr spectroscopy" or "colorimetry" or "immunofluorescence". If the variableMeasured is "depression rating", the measurementTechnique could be "Zung Scale" or "HAM-D" or "Beck Depression Inventory". If there are several variableMeasured properties recorded for some given data object, use a PropertyValue for each variableMeasured and attach the corresponding measurementTechnique. The value can also be from an enumeration, organized as a MeasurementMetholdEnumeration.

properties.label: measurementTechnique
properties.description: A technique, method or technology used in an Observation, StatisticalVariable or Dataset (or DataDownload, DataCatalog), corresponding to the method used for measuring the corresponding variable(s) (for datasets, described using variableMeasured; for Observation, a StatisticalVariable). Often but not necessarily each variableMeasured will have an explicit representation as (or mapping to) an property such as those defined in Schema.org, or other RDF vocabularies and "knowledge graphs". In that case the subproperty of variableMeasured called measuredProperty is applicable. The measurementTechnique property helps when extra clarification is needed about how a measuredProperty was measured. This is oriented towards scientific and scholarly dataset publication but may have broader applicability; it is not intended as a full representation of measurement, but can often serve as a high level summary for dataset discovery. For example, if variableMeasured is: molecule concentration, measurementTechnique could be: "mass spectrometry" or "nmr spectroscopy" or "colorimetry" or "immunofluorescence". If the variableMeasured is "depression rating", the measurementTechnique could be "Zung Scale" or "HAM-D" or "Beck Depression Inventory". If there are several variableMeasured properties recorded for some given data object, use a PropertyValue for each variableMeasured and attach the corresponding measurementTechnique. The value can also be from an enumeration, organized as a MeasurementMetholdEnumeration.

properties.label: variableMeasured
properties.description: The variableMeasured property can indicate (repeated as necessary) the variables that are measured in some dataset, either described as text or as pairs of identifier and description using PropertyValue, or more explicitly as a StatisticalVariable.
